ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, PA and PB are tangent to circle \(O\) at points A and B, respectively. Point E is a point on circle \(O\), and \(\angle AEB = 60^\circ\). What is the measure of \(\angle P\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw OA, BO;\\
Since $\angle AOB = 2\angle E = 120^{\circ}$,\\
thus $\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^{\circ}$,\\
therefore $\angle P = 180^{\circ} - \angle AOB = \boxed{60^{\circ}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, PA and PB are tangent to circle \(O\) at points A and B, respectively. Point E is a point on circle \(O\), and \(\angle AEB = 60^\circ\). What is the measure of \(\angle P\)?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Draw OA, BO;\\ Since $\angle AOB = 2\angle E = 120^{\circ}$,\\ thus $\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^{\circ}$,\\ therefore $\angle P = 180^{\circ} - \angle AOB = \boxed{60^{\circ}}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, with the center labeled O; point P is on the right side of the circle, and line segments PA and PB from P respectively touch the circle at the upper point A and the lower point B; point E is on the circumference on the left side of the circle, EA and EB are connected, and ∠AEB = 60° is marked in the figure. Then reason: According to the problem statement, PA and PB are two tangents to circle O, and E is on the circle. ∠AEB is an inscribed angle, and what it intercepts is arc AB not containing E, namely the smaller arc AB on the right side in the figure. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of arc AB is 2 × 60° = 120°. The exterior angle formed by two tangents is equal to half the difference of the measures of the two intercepted arcs, therefore ∠P = 1/2[(360° - 120°) - 120°] = 1/2 × 120° = 60°.
